messages:
bigretail_prod: Hey @luis — heads up from a customer on Android. They open a /v1/stream chat session, get ~3 partial SSE events (~1s apart) then the stream abruptly ends. Client shows a 401 in the fetch layer, but our server logs show no 401 returned on that connection. Request id: req_b5c7d2. Happens mostly on longer responses (20-40s).

luis (support): Sorry — can you paste the client-side error? Also does the app use short-lived session tokens or standard API keys? Any proxy/gateway in front?

bigretail_prod: Client console: 
```
fetch error: HTTP 401 Unauthorized
EventSource polyfill: connection closed unexpectedly
App-log: Stream aborted after 3 events
Network: LTE -> wifi handover noted right after last event
```
They use short-lived session tokens (15m) minted by their auth service and passed as Bearer in Authorization header. No extra gateway.

priya (eng): Two possibilities: (1) the client's token expired and their SDK attempted a refresh which triggered a new session creation and closed the underlying TCP connection, which the client perceives as 401, or (2) the mobile network handoff produced a TCP reset and their SDK mistakenly shows 401 from cached error. We should gather server-side wire logs for req_b5c7d2 and the auth service logs covering the session window.

sam (oncall): I pulled our edge logs for req_b5c7d2: we see a normal 200 with streaming body up to byte offset ~1024, then FIN from our side? No — we have a GET keepalive and then no further bytes. I don't see a 401 or 5xx. Upstream NAT shows a connection close from the client IP at 20.3s, flagged as tcp_fin from client. That usually indicates the client closed socket.

bigretail_prod: Interesting. Their backend auth service shows a token re-issue at 20.1s for that user (they rotate tokens on each activity). So token refresh coincides with the tcp_fin. They said their SDK rotates token by calling their auth endpoint and then re-sends new Authorization header on a new EventSource -> which would close the old stream.

luis (support): So the root cause seems client-side token rotation. Two high-impact mitigations: (A) avoid rotating session tokens while a stream is active (recommend keeping a stream-specific token TTL >= maximum expected stream duration), or (B) implement resume semantics so the client can reconnect and resume from partial prefix (Last-Event-ID) when rotation happens.

priya (eng): From our side we can also help:
- Recommend using a signed, non-rotating ephemeral token for SSE lasting e.g. 30-60m for streaming sessions.
- Add a server-side advisory: when we detect rapid client reconnects from same user within X seconds and matching session id, we can accept a short-lived `Last-Event-ID` to replay from a recent prefix cache (we already keep small prefix caches for cold-start resume).

bigretail_prod: Can you confirm whether a re-auth request from the client (to their auth provider) could trigger OS-level socket close causing our observed tcp_fin? Or is it purely their client JS aborting the connection?

sam (oncall): If the client JS aborts the fetch/EventSource to re-create a connection with a new header, you'd see a FIN from the client. If the OS drops the socket during a network handoff, you'll often see RST. Logs show FIN here, so the app-level logic closed the stream.

bigretail_prod: That matches — their SDK explicitly tears down SSE when it believes credentials rotated. We told them to avoid that for now.

priya (eng): Additional notes: some polyfills attempt to silently attach new headers by opening a new connection without resuming; that results in dropped output for users mid-stream. We should document best practices in our support KB:
- Use long-lived streaming token or signed URL param for streams
- If rotating tokens, do not close active streams; prefer a renewal endpoint or a separate short control channel to signal token updates
- Implement client retry with Last-Event-ID and exponential backoff

luis (support): Customer applied the change: they increased stream token TTL to 1 hour and modified SDK to defer token rotation until stream close. They retested on Android with LTE->wifi toggles. Out of 50 runs, 49 completed to [DONE]. One failure was a carrier drop (RST).

deploy-bot: Feature-flag toggled -> support/streaming-ttl-suggestion applied to KB for acct_bigretail by priya; expiry +72h

bigretail_prod: Thanks all. Could we get an internal note on edge behavior when clients close vs OS RST so we can triage faster next time? The difference between FIN and RST was super helpful.

sam (oncall): Will send a short runbook: how to interpret tcp_fin vs tcp_rst in our edge logs, and correlate with auth service events and token rotate timestamps. Tagging @priya to add the resume-prefix option to roadmap.

luis (support): Closing for now — reopen if we see continued truncations. :thumbsup:
